questions.explanation: A choice between two things uses "or".

options.text: The cat is on the mat

options.text: The cat is on the mat.

questions.questionText: Which sentence about the ducks is correct?
questions.explanation: For five ducks, we say "There are...".

questions.questionText: Which sentence about what she can do is correct?
questions.explanation: After "can", the word stays the same.

options.text: Dot has a red coat and an blue hat.

questions.questionText: ___ you like the story?

questions.questionText: Look! The little girl ___ a yellow dress.

questions.questionText: The garden looks very b___ today. Pick the correct spelling.

questions.questionText: Pick the British spelling.
questions.explanation: British English keeps the "u": "favourite".

questions.questionText: A word that means the same as "happy" is ___.
questions.explanation: "Glad" means happy.

questions.questionText: The opposite of "open" is ___.
questions.explanation: The opposite of open is shut.

questions.questionText: A baby dog is a puppy. A baby cat is a ___.
questions.explanation: A baby cat is a kitten.

questions.questionText: The little mouse "nibbles" the pie. That means it eats it ___.
questions.explanation: To nibble is to take tiny bites.

questions.explanation: To glow is to give a soft light.

questions.questionText: It is raining hard in the story. What does Peri need?
questions.explanation: In the rain, Peri needs a raincoat.

questions.questionText: The gate is locked and the goat wants to go inside. What will he do?
questions.explanation: A locked gate needs help from someone with the key.

questions.questionText: Dot plants a seed and waters it every day. After many days, what will she see?
questions.explanation: A watered seed grows into a small green shoot.

questions.questionText: Your teacher asks you to say a little rhyme in class. What do you do?
questions.explanation: We say the rhyme so everyone can hear.

questions.questionText: You want to show your picture to a friend. What do you say?
questions.explanation: We point out our picture and ask a friend to look.

questions.questionText: Which word has the same a-e sound as 'lake'?
questions.explanation: Lake and cave both have the a-e sound.

questions.questionText: Find the word with the ir sound, like 'girl'.
questions.explanation: Girl and first both have the ir sound.

questions.questionText: Which word has the 'air' sound, like 'hair'?
questions.explanation: Hair and bear both have the air sound; deer and hear have ear.

questions.questionText: Which animal lives in the sea?
questions.explanation: A whale lives in the sea.

questions.questionText: A very dry, sandy place with little water is a ___.
questions.explanation: A desert is a dry, sandy habitat.

questions.questionText: Which animal hops and carries its baby in a pouch?
questions.explanation: A kangaroo hops and carries its baby in a pouch.

questions.questionText: The natural home of an animal is called its ___.
questions.explanation: An animal's natural home is its habitat.

questions.questionText: You are at the zoo. A friend says, 'Look! A baby koala!' What do you say?
questions.explanation: We show interest when someone points out something exciting.

questions.questionText: A classmate asks, 'Can you name this animal?' and shows you a penguin. What do you answer?
questions.explanation: The question asks for the animal's name.

questions.questionText: Your friend says, 'Let's visit the bird park this Saturday.' What do you say?
questions.explanation: We agree to a 'Let's...' suggestion with a short accepting reply.

questions.questionText: Someone asks, 'Where does a polar bear live?' What do you answer?

options.label: C
options.text: It lives in the snow and ice.

questions.explanation: The question asks about the place where it lives.

questions.questionText: You want to ask your teacher about an animal. What do you say?

options.label: D
options.text: Excuse me, can you help me? What does a panda eat?

questions.explanation: We ask for help politely before a question.

questions.questionText: A friend says, 'I don't like spiders. They are scary.' What can you say to be kind?

options.label: A
options.text: I understand, but they help the garden.

questions.explanation: We respond politely and add a gentle, true fact.

questions.questionText: The teacher says, 'Now, work in pairs and talk about your favourite animal.' What do you do first?

options.label: B
options.text: Turn to your partner and ask about their favourite animal.

questions.explanation: Working in pairs means talking with the person next to you.

questions.questionText: Look at the ocean sentence. Which is correct?

options.text: There am a whale in the ocean.

options.label: C
options.text: There is a whale in the ocean.

options.label: D

questions.questionText: Look at the parrot sentence. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: We use 'These' when we talk about several birds.

questions.questionText: ___ many penguins are there in the group?

questions.questionText: Choose the correct answer. '___ a shark in the sea?' - 'Yes, there is.'
questions.explanation: We say 'Is there...?' when we ask about one thing.

questions.questionText: A new student asks, 'What animals do we see at the zoo?' What do you say?

options.label: C

questions.questionText: Your friend wants to know your favourite wild animal. What do you say?

options.label: D
options.text: My favourite animal is the giraffe.

options.label: A
options.text: It is black and white, and it cannot fly but it swims well.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a big green fruit.

questions.questionText: Someone asks, 'Can a kangaroo fly?' What do you answer?
questions.explanation: Kangaroos hop; they cannot fly.

questions.questionText: At the animal shop, you want to ask for help. What do you say?

options.label: C
options.text: Excuse me, can you tell me about this goat?

questions.explanation: We ask politely for information.

questions.questionText: Your little brother is scared of the snake behind the glass. What do you say?

options.label: B
options.text: The snake is very close now.

options.label: C
options.text: I do not like snakes either.

options.label: D
options.text: Do not worry, it is behind the glass. It cannot hurt us.

questions.explanation: We calm someone with a safe, kind explanation.

questions.questionText: Look at the cheetah sentence. Which is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: A cheetah can run very fast.

options.label: B
options.text: A cheetah cans run very fast.

options.label: C
options.text: A cheetah can runs very fast.

options.label: D
options.text: A cheetah can running very fast.

questions.explanation: After 'can' we use the simple form of the action word.

questions.questionText: Look at the parrot branch sentence. Which is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Look! The parrot sitting on the branch.

options.label: B
options.text: Look! The parrot is sitting on the branch.

options.label: C
options.text: Look! The parrot is sit on the branch.

options.label: D
options.text: Look! The parrot are sitting on the branch.

questions.explanation: We say 'is' plus the action word ending in -ing.

questions.questionText: Look at the panda question. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: We use 'Do' when we ask about several animals, and the action word stays simple.

questions.questionText: Look at the dolphin show sentence. Which is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Let's to watch the dolphin show.

questions.explanation: After 'Let's' we use the simple form of the action word.

questions.questionText: A whale lives in the ___.
questions.explanation: Whales live in the ocean.

questions.questionText: A giraffe has a very big ___.
questions.explanation: A giraffe has a very big neck.

questions.questionText: Kangaroos ___ across the grassland.
questions.explanation: Kangaroos hop across the ground.

questions.questionText: The polar bear has thick white ___.
questions.explanation: A polar bear has thick fur to keep warm.

questions.questionText: The elephant is big ___ gentle.
questions.explanation: 'But' links two different ideas about the elephant.

questions.questionText: Look at the monkey tree sentence. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: We say who does the action first, then what they do, then what it is done to.

questions.questionText: Look at the zoo camel sentence. Which is correct?

options.text: We saw at the zoo a camel.

options.label: B
options.text: A camel we saw the zoo.

options.label: C
options.text: We saw a camel at the zoo.

options.label: D

options.label: B
options.text: These animal come from the jungle.

options.label: C
options.text: This animals come from the jungle.

options.label: D
options.text: These animals come from the jungle.

questions.explanation: We use 'These' when we talk about several animals, so the action word does not add -s.

questions.questionText:

Where does Pip live?

questions.questionText:
Pip is a penguin. He lives on the cold, white ice. He has black and white feathers. Pip cannot fly, but he swims very well. He dives into the sea for food with many other penguins.
What can Pip do well?
questions.explanation: The text says Pip cannot fly, but he swims very well.

questions.questionText:
Balu is a camel. He lives in the hot, dry desert. He has a big hump on his back. The hump stores food for his walks across the sand. Balu can go many days without water. He walks across the hot sand under the bright sun.
Where does Balu live?
questions.explanation: The text says Balu lives in the hot, dry desert.

questions.questionText:
Balu is a camel. He lives in the hot, dry desert. He has a big hump on his back. The hump stores food for his walks across the sand. Balu can go many days without water. He walks across the hot sand under the bright sun.
Why does Balu have a hump?

options.label: D
options.text: It stores food for his walks.

questions.explanation: The text says the hump stores food for his walks.

questions.questionText:

Where is the reef?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says the reef is under the blue sea.

questions.questionText:
The reef is under the blue sea. Many small sea animals swim between the corals. A slow turtle hides in the rocks. A small crab cleans the turtle's back. Big sharks swim far away in the deep water. The reef is a busy, bright home.
What does the small crab do?
questions.explanation: The text says a small crab cleans the turtle's back.

options.label: C
options.text: It calls from a tall tree.

questions.explanation: The text says a parrot calls from a tall tree.

questions.questionText:
Deep in the green jungle, a parrot calls from a tall tree. A monkey jumps from branch to branch. Big leaves cover the wet ground. Bright flowers open when the sun rises. Many small insects fly near the flowers. The jungle is always warm and noisy.
How is the jungle described?
questions.explanation: The last sentence says the jungle is always warm and noisy.

questions.questionText:

What covers the trees in winter?
questions.explanation: The text says snow covers the tall trees.

questions.questionText:
It is winter in the forest. Snow covers the tall trees. A small deer looks for dry leaves under a tree. Her brown coat keeps her warm. Birds fly south to find food. The forest is quiet and white until the warm days return.
Why do the birds fly south?
questions.explanation: The text says birds fly south to find food.

questions.questionText:

questions.explanation: The text says a swan swims on the quiet lake.

questions.questionText:
On the quiet lake, a swan swims slowly. Her curved neck reaches down for plants under the water. Two small babies swim behind her. Dragonflies sit on the green leaves. The water is still and blue in the early hours.
What does the swan reach down for?
questions.explanation: The text says her curved neck reaches down for plants under the water.

questions.questionText:

'He has black and white feathers.' 'Feathers' cover a ___.

questions.questionText: We climb up and down between floors on these. What are they?
questions.explanation: Stairs take us up and down between floors.

questions.questionText: A classmate says to you: 'Sorry, I am late.' What do you say?
questions.explanation: When someone says sorry, we reply 'That's all right.'

questions.questionText: You want a pencil from your teacher. What do you say?

options.label: A
options.text: Can I have a pencil, please?

questions.explanation: We ask politely: 'Can I have something, please?'

questions.questionText: Your friend wants to play football with you. What is a good reply?
questions.explanation: 'Good idea!' answers a Let's suggestion.

questions.questionText: Someone asks: 'Is there a kitchen in your house?' What do you answer?
questions.explanation: We answer 'Is there...?' with 'Yes, there is.'

questions.questionText: You do not hear your friend. What do you say?
questions.explanation: We say 'Pardon?' to ask someone to repeat.

questions.questionText: Your mother says: 'It is time for bed.' What do you say?
questions.explanation: At bedtime we say 'Good night.'

questions.questionText: You drop your books and a classmate helps you pick them up. What do you say?
questions.explanation: We thank someone who helps us.

questions.questionText: About one book on a chair. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: There are a book on the chair.

options.label: B
options.text: There is books on the chair.

options.label: C
options.text: There is a book on the chair.

options.label: D
options.text: There am a book on the chair.

questions.explanation: We say 'There is' for one thing (a book).

questions.questionText: About two windows. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: There is two windows in the hall.

options.label: B
options.text: There are two window in the hall.

options.label: C
options.text: There am two windows in the hall.

options.label: D
options.text: There are two windows in the hall.

questions.explanation: We use 'There are' for two windows.

questions.questionText: '___ any shelves in the cellar?' Choose the correct words.
questions.explanation: 'Any' with shelves takes 'Are there...?'

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence about several towels.

options.label: A
options.text: There is some towels in the bathroom.

options.label: B
options.text: There are some towels in the bathroom.

options.label: C
options.text: There are some towel in the bathroom.

options.label: D
options.text: There are any towels in the bathroom.

questions.explanation: We use 'there are' with 'some' for things like towels.

questions.questionText: A new classmate says: 'Hello! My name is Arif. What is your name?' What do you say?

options.label: B
options.text: I am nine years old too.

questions.explanation: We answer a name question with our own name.

questions.questionText: Your friend asks: 'Can you swim?' Choose the true reply for a boy who can swim.
questions.explanation: We answer 'Can you...?' with 'Yes, I can.'

questions.questionText: Your teacher asks: 'How many rooms are there in your house?' You count four rooms. What do you say?
questions.explanation: We answer 'How many...?' with 'There are' plus a number and a word like 'rooms'.

questions.questionText: Your little sister cannot find her hat. She asks: 'Where is my hat?' You see it under the bed. What do you say?

options.label: B
options.text: It is in the bedroom, under the bed.

questions.explanation: We answer 'Where is...?' with 'It is in...' plus the place.

questions.questionText: You want to open the window but it is stuck. You ask a friend for help. What do you say?
questions.explanation: We ask for help politely with 'Can you help me, please?'

questions.questionText: A friend says: 'Let's go to the park on Saturday.' You do not want to go. What do you say politely?

options.label: D
options.text: Sorry, I can't. I help at home on Saturday.

questions.explanation: We refuse a suggestion politely and say why.

questions.questionText: About playing football on Saturdays. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: D
options.text: I am play football on Saturdays.

questions.explanation: After 'I', we say 'play', not 'plays'.

questions.questionText: '___ your brother play football after school?' Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: For 'your brother' (he), we use 'Does...?'

questions.questionText: About a pair of socks. Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: 'These' goes with words like 'socks'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence. Your sister has a red dress on now.

options.label: C
options.text: She are wearing a red dress.

options.label: D
options.text: She is wearing a red dress.

questions.explanation: We say 'She is wearing...' for what someone has on now.

questions.questionText: I ___ my room on Saturday. Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: After 'I', we say 'clean', not 'cleans'.

questions.questionText: There ___ four chairs in the dining room. Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: 'Four chairs' is not just one, so we use 'are'.

questions.questionText: How many ___ are there in your kitchen?
questions.explanation: 'How many' goes with words like 'windows'.

questions.questionText: My brother ___ television in the living room now.
questions.explanation: For 'my brother' (he), we use 'is watching'.

questions.questionText: We play in the park ___ Saturday morning. Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' with days: on Saturday.

questions.questionText: About helping mum in the kitchen. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: I my mother help in the kitchen.

options.label: B
options.text: I help my mother in the kitchen.

options.label: C
options.text: In the kitchen I my mother help.

options.label: D
options.text: Help I my mother in the kitchen.

questions.explanation: We say 'I' first, then what we do, then the place.

questions.questionText: About a toy bear on the stairs. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: My toy bear under the stairs sleeps.

options.label: B
options.text: Under the stairs my toy bear sleeps.

options.label: C
options.text: My toy bear sleeps under the stairs.

options.label: D
options.text: Sleeps my toy bear under the stairs.

questions.explanation: We say who it is and what it does first, then the place.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence about ability.

options.label: A
options.text: I can rides my bike in the park.

options.label: B
options.text: I riding can my bike in the park.

options.label: C
options.text: Can I ride my bike in the park?

options.label: D
options.text: I can ride my bike in the park.

questions.explanation: 'Can' stays the same, and we say the action word after it.

questions.questionText: Which word has the 'i-e' sound, as in 'kite'?
questions.explanation: Nine has the 'i-e' sound.

questions.questionText: Choose the word with the 'o-e' sound, like 'rose'.
questions.explanation: Nose has the 'o-e' sound.

questions.questionText: Find the word that begins with the 'wh' sound.
questions.explanation: White begins with 'wh'.

questions.questionText: Choose the word with the 'ph' sound, like 'phone'.
questions.explanation: Photo has 'ph' making the /f/ sound.

questions.questionText: Which word ends with the 'ay' sound, as in 'day'?
questions.explanation: Play ends with 'ay'.

questions.questionText: Which word has the 'ea' sound, like 'tea'?
questions.explanation: 'Sea' has the same 'ea' sound as 'tea'.

questions.questionText: Find the word with the 'ou' sound, like 'house'.
questions.explanation: Out has the 'ou' sound.

questions.questionText: Choose the word with the 'ir' sound.
questions.explanation: Girl has the 'ir' sound.

questions.questionText: Pick the word that has the 'air' sound, like 'hair'.
questions.explanation: Chair has the 'air' sound.

questions.questionText: Choose the word with the 'oy' sound.
questions.explanation: Toy has the 'oy' sound.

questions.questionText: Find the word with the 'aw' sound, like 'draw'.
questions.explanation: Saw has the 'aw' sound.

questions.questionText: Find the word with the 'ew' sound, like 'few'.
questions.explanation: New has the 'ew' sound.

questions.questionText: Choose the word with the 'u-e' sound, like 'huge'.
questions.explanation: 'Mule' has the same 'u-e' sound as 'huge'.

questions.questionText: Which word has the 'au' sound, as in 'August'?
questions.explanation: Autumn has the 'au' sound.

questions.questionText: About a room with a bath. Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: We spell it b-a-t-h-r-o-o-m.

questions.questionText: About the room you cook in. Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: We spell it k-i-t-c-h-e-n.

questions.questionText: About the start of the weekend. Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Saturday has a 'u' after the t: S-a-t-u-r-d-a-y.

questions.questionText: (BrE) About a red colour. Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: BrE spelling is c-o-l-o-u-r.

questions.questionText: About a castle made of sand. Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: We spell it s-a-n-d-c-a-s-t-l-e.

questions.questionText: About steps between floors. Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Stairs (the steps) is s-t-a-i-r-s; 'stares' is a different word.

questions.questionText:
Daniel lives in a small house. Upstairs, his bedroom is next to the bathroom. Downstairs, the kitchen is behind the dining room. His mother reads in the living room. Daniel leaves his bag on the stairs.

Where is Daniel's bedroom?
questions.explanation: The passage says his bedroom is next to the bathroom.

questions.questionText:
Daniel lives in a small house. Upstairs, his bedroom is next to the bathroom. Downstairs, the kitchen is behind the dining room. His mother reads in the living room. Daniel leaves his bag on the stairs.

What does Daniel's mother do in the living room?
questions.explanation: His mother reads in the living room.

questions.questionText:
On Saturdays, Ben wakes up late. He helps his dad clean the windows. After lunch, he rides his bike in the park. In the evening, Ben paints a picture. He feels happy.

What does Ben do after lunch?

options.label: B
options.text: He paints a picture at noon

options.label: C
options.text: He rides his bike in the park

questions.explanation: After lunch, Ben rides his bike in the park.

questions.questionText:
On Saturdays, Ben wakes up late. He helps his dad clean the windows. After lunch, he rides his bike in the park. In the evening, Ben paints a picture. He feels happy.

When does Ben clean the windows?
questions.explanation: On Saturdays he cleans the windows before lunch, in the morning.

questions.questionText:
Ivan goes to the beach with his family. The sun is hot and the sand is warm. Ivan makes a big sandcastle. He plays in the water. His dad takes a photo. They eat ice cream at noon.

What does Ivan make at the beach?
questions.explanation: Ivan makes a big sandcastle.

questions.questionText:
Ivan goes to the beach with his family. The sun is hot and the sand is warm. Ivan makes a big sandcastle. He plays in the water. His dad takes a photo. They eat ice cream at noon.

When do Ivan and his family eat ice cream?
questions.explanation: They eat ice cream at noon.

questions.questionText:
Yuki visits her grandmother's old house. The house has a dark cellar and tall stairs. Yuki does not go to the cellar. She looks out of the window and watches the birds. Grandmother smiles and gives her a cup of tea.

Yuki does not go to the cellar. What is the cellar like?
questions.explanation: The cellar is dark, so Yuki does not go there.

questions.questionText:
Yuki visits her grandmother's old house. The house has a dark cellar and tall stairs. Yuki does not go to the cellar. She looks out of the window and watches the birds. Grandmother smiles and gives her a cup of tea.

What does Yuki do at the window?
questions.explanation: Yuki looks out of the window and watches the birds.

questions.questionText:
Ryan sets the table in the dining room. His sister cooks rice in the kitchen. Their dad mops the hall. Ryan then watches television in the living room. It is a busy Saturday afternoon.

Where does Ryan's sister cook the rice?
questions.explanation: His sister cooks rice in the kitchen.

questions.questionText:
Ryan sets the table in the dining room. His sister cooks rice in the kitchen. Their dad mops the hall. Ryan then watches television in the living room. It is a busy Saturday afternoon.

Who mops the hall?
questions.explanation: Their dad mops the hall.

questions.questionText:
It is a rainy Saturday. Rafi cannot go out. He builds a tall tower with his blocks in the bedroom. His sister reads a book on the bed. When the rain stops, they run to the window and look at the wet stairs.

Why can Rafi not go out?
questions.explanation: It is a rainy Saturday, so Rafi cannot go out.

questions.questionText:
It is a rainy Saturday. Rafi cannot go out. He builds a tall tower with his blocks in the bedroom. His sister reads a book on the bed. When the rain stops, they run to the window and look at the wet stairs.

What do Rafi and his sister look at after the rain stops?
questions.explanation: They look at the wet stairs.

questions.questionText:
Daniel lives in a small house. Upstairs, his bedroom is next to the bathroom. Downstairs, the kitchen is behind the dining room. His mother reads in the living room. Daniel leaves his bag on the stairs.

In the story, 'next to the bathroom' means the bedroom is ___ the bathroom.
questions.explanation: 'Next to' means beside.

questions.questionText:
On Saturdays, Ben wakes up late. He helps his dad clean the windows. After lunch, he rides his bike in the park. In the evening, Ben paints a picture. He feels happy.

'Ben wakes up late' means Ben ___.
questions.explanation: 'Wakes up' means opens your eyes and gets out of bed.

questions.questionText:
Ivan goes to the beach with his family. The sun is hot and the sand is warm. Ivan makes a big sandcastle. He plays in the water. His dad takes a photo. They eat ice cream at noon.

'The sand is warm' means the sand is ___.
questions.explanation: 'Warm' means a little hot, not cold.

questions.questionText:
Yuki visits her grandmother's old house. The house has a dark cellar and tall stairs. Yuki does not go to the cellar. She looks out of the window and watches the birds. Grandmother smiles and gives her a cup of tea.

'A dark cellar' means the cellar has ___.
questions.explanation: 'Dark' means there is little or no light.

questions.questionText:
Ryan sets the table in the dining room. His sister cooks rice in the kitchen. Their dad mops the hall. Ryan then watches television in the living room. It is a busy Saturday afternoon.

'It is a busy afternoon' means ___.

options.label: A
options.text: there are many things to do

questions.explanation: 'Busy' means you have many things to do.

questions.questionText:
It is a rainy Saturday. Rafi cannot go out. He builds a tall tower with his blocks in the bedroom. His sister reads a book on the bed. When the rain stops, they run to the window and look at the wet stairs.

'The wet stairs' means the stairs are ___.
questions.explanation: After rain, the stairs are wet, with water on them.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence with a capital letter and a full stop.

options.label: A
options.text: i clean my room on saturday

options.label: B
options.text: I clean my room on saturday.

options.label: C
options.text: I clean my room on Saturday.

options.label: D
options.text: I clean my room on Saturday

questions.questionText: We have dinner ___ the dining room. Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: We say 'in the dining room.'

questions.questionText: In the kitchen we have a table ___ four chairs. Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: We join two nouns with 'and'.

questions.questionText: Do you want tea ___ milk? Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: We offer a choice with 'or'.

questions.questionText: The room is small ___ clean. Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: 'But' shows a contrast: small, yet clean.

questions.questionText: About a window in the bedroom. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: There a window is in my bedroom.

options.label: B
options.text: In my bedroom there a window is.

options.label: C
options.text: Is there a window in my bedroom.

options.label: D
options.text: There is a window in my bedroom.

questions.explanation: We say 'There is a...' and then the place.

questions.questionText: About cleaning the car. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: I help my dad clean the car.

options.label: B
options.text: I help my dad the car clean.

options.label: C
options.text: Clean the car I help my dad.

options.label: D
options.text: My dad I help clean the car.

questions.explanation: Word order: I, then help my dad, then clean the car.

questions.questionText: Asking about rooms in a house. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: How many room are there in your house?

options.label: B
options.text: How many rooms are there in your house?

options.label: C
options.text: How many rooms there are in your house?

options.label: D
options.text: How many is rooms in your house?

questions.explanation: 'How many' goes with words like 'rooms', and we say 'are there'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence. Your brother can ride a bike.

options.label: A
options.text: My brother can rides a bike.

options.label: B
options.text: My brother cans ride a bike.

options.label: C
options.text: My brother can ride a bike.

options.label: D
options.text: Can ride my brother a bike.

questions.explanation: 'Can' stays the same and we say the action word after it.

questions.questionText: Asking about watching television. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: Does you watch television at the weekend?

options.label: B
options.text: Do you watches television at the weekend?

options.label: C
options.text: Are you watch television at the weekend?

options.label: D
options.text: Do you watch television at the weekend?

questions.explanation: With 'you', we use 'Do you...?'

questions.questionText: '___ there any stairs in your house?' Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: 'Stairs' is not just one step, so we use 'Are there...?'

questions.questionText: About seeing a mouse in the kitchen. Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: I can sees a mouse in the kitchen.

options.label: B
options.text: I can see a mouse in the kitchen.

options.label: C
options.text: I can seeing a mouse in the kitchen.

options.label: D
options.text: I cans see a mouse in the kitchen.

questions.explanation: After 'can', we say 'see', not 'sees'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence about one towel and two books.

options.label: A
options.text: There are a towel and there is two books.

options.label: B
options.text: There is a towel and there is two books.

options.label: C
options.text: There is a towel and there are two books.

options.label: D
options.text: There are a towel and there are two books.

questions.explanation: A towel takes 'there is'; two books takes 'there are'.

questions.questionText: About glass you look through. Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: We spell it w-i-n-d-o-w.

questions.questionText: (BrE) About someone who lives next door. Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: BrE spelling is n-e-i-g-h-b-o-u-r.

questions.questionText: About a room you sleep in. Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: We spell it b-e-d-r-o-o-m.

questions.questionText: A chant goes: 'Clean your hands and wipe the plate.' Which action word is in it?
questions.explanation: 'Clean' is the action word in the chant.

questions.questionText: Our chant goes: 'Paint a picture, paint it red.' Which thing do we paint?
questions.explanation: We paint a picture; 'red' tells the colour.

questions.questionText: In a simple rhyme about a home, which word names the steps you climb up?
questions.explanation: Stairs are the steps you climb up.

questions.questionText: The chant says: 'Busy hands, busy feet.' What does 'busy' tell us?
questions.explanation: 'Busy' means doing many things.

questions.questionText: 'The old house has a deep dark hall.' What does 'old' tell us about the house?
questions.explanation: 'Old' means it has existed for many years, not new.

questions.questionText: The chant says the sun is hot and the sand is warm. Where are the children?
questions.explanation: Hot sun and warm sand tell us they are at the beach.

questions.questionText: It is raining hard. Rafi looks out of the window. What will he probably do?

options.label: B
options.text: Ride his bike in the park

questions.explanation: On a rainy day we stay inside.

questions.questionText: Yuki says: 'I want a drink, but the cups are in the kitchen.' Where does she need to go?
questions.explanation: The cups are in the kitchen, so she goes there.

questions.questionText: Your friend sings a rhyme with you. At the end, what do you say?
questions.explanation: We share a happy feeling after a rhyme.

questions.questionText: You make up a short chant for your class. What do you do first?

options.label: A
options.text: Shout as loud as you can

questions.explanation: We say chant words clearly so everyone can hear.
